title: MightyKids, Families & Community (MightyKFC)

sections.About this support:

- Centre based activities
- Life skills workshops
- Individual mentoring
- Community service
- Parent-child bonding session
sections.Who is this for?:
- MightyKFC’s client group is latchkey children and youth from the lower income group, aged 4 – 16 years old.
- MightyKFC targets children and youth who primarily reside or study in schools in the Telok Blangah region.
sections.How to apply?:
You may:

- Walk into the centre
- Email to [mkfc@life-community.org](mailto:mkfc@life-community.org)
- Call the centre at [62707198](tel:62707198)
sections.What to expect?:
- An intake interview will be arranged to register for the programme.
- Upon successful registration, services will be provided to the service users for the duration of the programme at the activity centre.

title: Babes Pregnancy Crisis Support
description: For individuals aged 21 and below needing support with their pregnancy, so that they are aware of their options and are able to make an informed decision regarding their pregnancy.

sections.About this support:
Babes supports pregnant teens through:

- Casework and counselling
- 24-hour helpline
- Practical support (befriender, baby essentials, employment & back to school assistance etc)
- Information & resources
- Outreach and youth engagement events
sections.Who is this for?:
- Pregnant teenager who needs help; Anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
sections.How to apply?: If you are a pregnant teen who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about teenage pregnancy, please contact Babes' 24-hour helpline at 6206 6641 or text via WhatsApp at 8111 3535 to speak to the caseworkers.
sections.What to expect?:
- Teenagers who require help with their pregnancy and/or anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy may contact Babes via the 24-hour helpline (call/text).
- When an enquiry is attended to, the Helpliner will also assess if the teenager is eligible to be a case under Babes. Should the assessment be one that Babes can assist, Babes will arrange for a meeting with the teenager and/or her family/partner within 3-5 working days to assess the needs and provide the necessary support and guidance.

title: SkillsFuture Credit
description: For Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above to pay for or offset the out-of-pocket course fees of approved courses.
highlights: SkillsFuture Credits can be used on top of existing SWDA course fee subsidies

sections.About this support:

- A one-off SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 was provided to every Singapore Citizen aged 25 and above as at 31 December 2020. These credits will expire on 31 December 2025.
- Can be used on top of existing government course subsidies to pay for a wide range of approved skills-related courses, such as:
  - Courses subsidised or approved by SkillsFuture Singapore including online courses
  - Selected courses offered by Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded institutions
  - Courses supported by lead agencies
  - SkillsFuture@PA courses offered by the People’s Association and selected courses under National Silver Academy
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen
- Aged 25 and above
sections.How to apply?:
- No application required
- How to use your SkillsFuture Credit:
  - Step 1: Inform your Training Provider that you intend to use your SkillsFuture Credit in part or in full for the qualifying course fees at the point of course registration
  - Step 2: Submit your claim via MySkillsFuture within 60 days before the course start date (date inclusive)

title: Workfare Skills Support (Level-Up)
description: Enhanced tier of Workfare Skills Support (WSS), supporting lower-wage Singaporean workers who go for long-form training.
highlights: Provides training allowance  of at least $300 per month
Covers a wide catalogue of long-form courses (including Nitec, Higher Nitec, Diplomas, Post-Diplomas, and Undergraduate courses)
Covers multiple bouts of long-form training
Apply online via the Training Allowance System using Singpass

sections.About this support:
**Training Allowance (TA)**

- Full-time training: 50% of average income over the latest available 12-month period, with minimum allowance of $300 per month
- Part-time training: $300 per month

**Coverage for multiple rounds of long-form training**

Every individual can receive:

- Up to 24 months of monthly TA between ages 30 to 39
- Up to another 24 months of monthly TA from age 40. This is a shared cap between WSS (Level-Up) and the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme
- For each age period, the cap is shared between both full-time and part-time training

**Courses supported include:**

- SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme courses
- Nitec, Higher Nitec, Diplomas, Post-Diplomas, and Undergraduate courses by Institutes of Higher Learning
- From 2026 Q4, long-form Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) full qualifications
sections.How to apply?: You can apply online via the [Training Allowance System (TAS)](https://go.gov.sg/wss-level-up-tas)** **using your Singpass.

title: Sheltered Workshops
description: Sheltered Workshops offer employment and/or vocational training to adults with disabilities who do not possess the competencies or skills for open employment.

sections.About this support:
Sheltered workshops offer the following:

- Employment and/or vocational training to adults with disabilities who do not possess the competencies or skills for open employment.
- Allow participants to practice in jobs or tasks where the processes are either simple or broken down into simpler steps.
- Participants will gain valuable experience at the workshop, thereby improving their prospects for open employment.
sections.Who is this for?:
Applicants should be:

- 18 years old and above*^#
- Singapore citizens of Permanent Residents^^
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.

*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.

^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.

#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.

^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.

**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)
sections.How to apply?:
- Please approach a social service professional from a Touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a Sheltered Workshop application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).
- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.

**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**

**Step 1:**

All applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.

**Step 2:**

If the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.

**Step 3:**

Registered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.

1. **Online submission (Recommended)**
  Log into e-Services using your CorpPass
2. **Hardcopy submission**
  Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:
  - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)
  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)
  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)
  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon receiving the referral, SG Enable will contact you to provide information to help you make an informed decision on your choice of service.
- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management.

title: Workfare Skills Support (WSS) (Basic)
description: Provides training allowance and cash incentives to encourage lower-wage Singaporean workers to upskill via training.
highlights: Provides training allowance for trainees who self-sponsor their own short training
Provides cash award for trainees who complete sustained training
Provides absentee payroll for employers who send eligible employees for training
No application required for employees; self-employed persons and employers should submit claims online

sections.About this support:
- Training Allowance (TA) of $10.50 per training hour for self-sponsored trainees
- Training commitment award of $800 for one Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) or Academic Continuing Education and Training Qualification
- Absentee payroll for employers sending eligible employees for training: 95% trainee’s basic hourly wage, capped at $13 per training hour
- WSS (Basic) supports short training, such as:
  - Eligible courses at the [MySkillsFuture Portal](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/portal-search/portal-search.html?fq=Course_Supp_Period_To_1:[2026-06-25T00:00:00Z TO *]&fq=IsValid:true&fq={!tag=Tags_text_Filtered}Tags_text_Filtered:("Workfare_Training Commitment" "Workfare_Training Allowance")&q=*:*&filtersearch=Tags_text_Filtered:)
  - Recommended courses that meet Progressive Wage Model (PWM) training requirements
sections.How to apply?:
**Employees**

No application needed.

** **

**Self-employed persons**

You will need to provide in the [TA claim form](https://go.gov.sg/wss-sep-ta) within 120 days of course end date:

- softcopy of your proof of self-employment (for example, contract for service or equivalent dated within 3 months after course end date, or ACRA business registration and business transaction documents dated within 3 months after course end date)
- your course details (for example, course title, course start and end dates, and training provider’s name

**Employers**

You can [apply online at Enterprise Portal for Jobs and Skills](https://sfec.enterprisejobskills.gov.sg/Callbackhandler/Prelogin.aspx)

title: SkillsFuture Advice
description: A webinar that helps you learn about SkillsFuture programmes, MySkillsFuture portal and funding support.
highlights: 1-hour webinar

sections.About this support:
Free 1-hour webinars that will guide you in developing your resilience and upskilling plans through practical information and online resources:

- Understand your resilience and find learning programmes/initiatives that suit your needs
- Learn practical tips on developing your resilience mindset, building a circle of social support and improving your employability by planning for the future

title: MyCareersFuture
description: The one-stop portal for job search and application needs. It uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to help jobseekers discover career opportunities, make career transitions, or search for jobs based on skills matches.  It also provides valuable career-related resources, including career insights and career guidance to facilitate their career planning and career development processes.
highlights: Our latest Job-to-Skills job matching algorithm connects you with opportunities tailored to your skills and experience.
Utilise CareersFinder to discover personalised upskilling and career recommendations based on your unique profile.
Filter jobs eligible for Government support such as Career Conversion Programmes, Graduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme and Mid-Career Pathways Programmes
Elevate your skills with our curated articles, webinars, and courses designed for your professional growth.

sections.About this support:
- **Advanced Matching Algorithm: **Our latest Job-to-Skills job matching algorithm connects you with opportunities tailored to your skills and experience.
- **CareersFinder by MyCareersFuture: **[CareersFinder](https://careersfinder.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/) harnesses Government data and artificial intelligence to help individuals discover personalised upskilling and career recommendations based on their unique profile to achieve their career goals.
- **Government Support Eligibility: **Filter jobs eligible for Government support such as:
  - Career Conversion Programmes (CCP) if you are open to reskill and change career/occupations
  - GRaduate Industry and Traineeship Programme (GRIT) if you are a fresh graduate looking for a traineeship opportunity, and
  - Mid-Career Pathways Programmes (MCPP) if you are a mature individual looking for a mid-career attachments.
- **CareersCompass by MyCareersFuture:** Access curated articles, career guides and expert insights to help you navigate career planning, skills development and job search strategies.
- **CareersHorizon by MyCareersFuture: **A one-stop digital platform for career-related event registrations and management. It enables Singaporeans to access a comprehensive suite of career resources, including online articles, virtual career events, seminars, and workshops. The platform also offers micro-learning content, such as podcasts, covering topics relevant to all career stages. Additionally, it supports Singaporeans in searching and registering for career events, and it also facilitates networking opportunities between employers and individuals.
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are looking to plan their careers, make career transitions, or search for jobs.
sections.How to apply?: Embark on your journey to professional success with [MyCareersFuture](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/).

sections.About this support:
- Access on-the-job training to switch careers into growth sectors with long-term prospects
- Salary support of up to 90% for mid-career workers
- Embark on a new career with CCPs across around 30 sectors
sections.Who is this for?:
Mid-career individuals should meet the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 21 or above
- Graduated or completed National Service, for at least 2 years
- Career conversion is required:
  - New Hire: New job role trained for under the CCP should be substantially different from previous job role before joining CCP
  - Existing Employee: New job role should be growth job roles identified under the Jobs Transformation Maps (JTMs)
- Able to commit to full-time employment or attachment in a participating company

Beyond the general eligibility criteria, different CCPs may have additional course-specific entry requirements, and employers may apply their own -specific shortlisting process. In general, individuals applying for CCPs should also not be shareholders, immediate ex-staff, or related to owners/decision-makers of the CCP participating company or its related entities.
sections.How to apply?: Apply for CCPs here through CCP-supportable jobs on [MyCareersFuture](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/).

sections.Who is this for?:

- Unemployed due to involuntary reasons such as retrenchment, cessation of business, dismissals or termination due to illness, injury or accident
- Lives in a property in Singapore with annual value of $31,000 or less

title: YMCA Vocational and Soft Skills Programme (VaSSP)
description: Aims to equip out-of-school youths and youths-at-risk with job competency as well as specific vocational skills.

sections.About this support:
The YMCA Vocational and Soft Skills Programme (VaSSP), also known as Project Bridge, aims to equip out-of-school youths and youths-at-risk of dropping out (who are absent from school for a long period) with essential soft skills and vocational expertise, enabling them to enhance their employability to integrate into the workforce or to reintegrate to education.

Conducted over 6 months, the programme consists to three phases: Core Training, Vocational Training, and Monitoring Phase. Service users engage in soft skills training, covering crucial areas such as goal setting, resume writing, interview skills, and communication and conflict resolution.

Subsequently, youths can select one out of 14 vocational tracks and receive certified training in the chosen industry. Thereafter, YMCA staff will continue to monitor the service users for a period of time before completion of the programme by supporting them in aspects such as career counselling or academic support in the service users' journey to either obtain employment or reintegrate back into education.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Unemployed youths or school leavers between 15 and 21 years old
- Educational attainment of 'N' levels or below
- Pass the admission interview
- Able to commit and attend full-time training, and achieve 75% attendance and above
sections.How to apply?:
- Email - projectbridge@ymca.org.sg
- Students can be referred by school counsellor or other social service agencies
sections.What to expect?:
- Interested parties can write in to VaSSP and a staff will be in touch within 3 working days
- Youths will need to go through admission interview and meet the criteria of the programme

description: Mentoring programme for youths-at-risk in Jurong.

sections.About this support: The GRIT Academy (TGA) aims to provide individual mentoring support for youths-at-risk aged between 11 to 17 years old residing or studying in schools in Jurong; and serve as the primary relationship holder to follow through with the youths as they transit to other youth programmes.
sections.Who is this for?:
The target clientele is youths-at-risk aged between 11 to 17 years old residing or studying in schools in Jurong (i.e. Jurong West, Jurong East and Taman Jurong).

Applicants must fulfil at least one of the following criteria to be eligible for the programme:

1. Youths who lack meaningful engagements such as those not attending Co-Curricular Activities, as well as youths who often loiter at public areas such as playgrounds and void decks.
2. Youths with underprivileged background such as youths from low-income families, students receiving the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme and youths staying in rental flats.
3. Youths exhibiting at-risk behaviour such as poor affiliation to schools, minor behavioural issues, socio-emotional issues and/or peer issues.
sections.How to apply?: Complete the form on https://lakeside.org.sg/our-services/the-grit-project/ and email it to [thegritproject@lakeside.org.sg](mailto:thegritproject@lakeside.org.sg).
sections.What to expect?: Screening for potential service users will take approximately 2 weeks from the referral/youth sign-up. Adjustment to the screening time frame will be considered based on the assessed urgency.

title: Enabling Business Hub
description: Developed by SG Enable, Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) bring training and employment opportunities closer to homes for persons with disabilities through customised job support and inclusive workplace practices.
highlights: Employment for PwDs
Training and employment opportunities for PwDs

sections.About this support:
With an on-site Employment Support Team, persons with disabilities can look forward to a comprehensive suite of employment-related services such as vocational assessment, training, job-matching and post-placement job support. These services aim to better match persons with disabilities to jobs in the region based on their skills and interests and support them in employment.

EBH@Jurong

Located beside Lakeside MRT, at 111A Yuan Ching Road, Singapore 619606, EBH@Jurong aims to bring training and employment opportunities closer to the homes of persons with disabilities living in the West, including those with higher work support needs.

Key Features of EBH@Jurong

1. Provide targeted training and support** **to prepare persons with disabilities for employment in the logistics sector.
2. Provide on-site employment support, including longer and more intensive employment support for persons with disabilities with higher work support needs and require a longer runway of support to work independently in the community.
sections.Who is this for?:
Applicants should be:

- Aged 16 and above
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
- Verified to have a permanent disability of any of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least one of the six Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism
- Preferably living in the West or keen to work in the Logistics industry
sections.How to apply?:
**Prior to application, applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into **[**SupportGoWhere**](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/status/pwdr)**. **

**Preparation of documents**

The following supporting documents are required before making an application:

- [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/disability-verification-form.pdf) (To be completed and endorsed by registered healthcare professional if disability status is unverified)
- Copy of NRIC Front and Back
- [One Referral Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/one-referral-form-with-omnibus_2025.pdf?sfvrsn=ab89bee_1) (For email/physical submissions only)

**How to apply**

Persons with disabilities seeking employment assistance may:

1. Apply online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/ebh/apply),[ ](#_msocom_5)or
2. Download the One Referral Form (ORF) and email the supporting documents to EBH@Jurong at [EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg](mailto:EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg) or;
3. Contact [EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg](mailto:EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg) to schedule an appointment with the EBH@Jurong employment services team.

Persons with disabilities keen on other employment programmes, please email us at [employment@sgenable.sg](mailto:employment@sgenable.sg).

title: Job Placement and Job Support
description: Provides persons with disabilities employment assistance through job matching and job coaching for up to 12 months.
highlights: Vocational assessment to assess work readiness
Explore job opportunities with inclusive employers

sections.About this support:
SG Enable works with partner agencies funded by the government to provide Job Placement and Job Support (JPJS) services such as APSN, Autism Resource Centre (Singapore), Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore (MINDS) and SPD. Persons with disabilities who approach SG Enable for employment assistance will be referred to a suitable partner agency, subject to the respective agency’s eligibility criteria.

SG Enable and its appointed partners provide specialised job placement and job support services that include the following:

- Assessing the jobseeker’s strengths, job interests and skills, and identifying training opportunities
- Helping the jobseeker identify job opportunities and link up with prospective inclusive employers
- Assessing the nature of the job and its tasks for suitability
- Assessing the built environment for accessibility
- Working with the employer to job redesign and recommend workplace modification, making use of assistive devices, if needed
- On-site job coaching to help the new employee integrate into the workplace
sections.Who is this for?:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are verified to have a permanent disability of any of the following:

- Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least one of the size Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
- Moderate Visual Impairment or worse in the better eye
- Moderate Hearing Loss or worse in the better ear
- Intellectual Disability
- Autism

^You can check if your disability status is verified on [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/status/pwdr) or contact us at [employment@sgenable.sg](mailto:employment@sgenable.sg).
sections.How to apply?:
**Preparation of documents**

The following support documents are required before making an application:

- [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/disability-verification-form.pdf) (To be completed and endorsed by registered healthcare professional)
- Copy of NRIC Front and Back
- One Referral Form (for email/physical submissions only)

**How to apply**

Persons with disabilities seeking employment assistance may apply

1)      Online via SupportGoWhere, or

2)      Download the [One Referral Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/one-referral-form-with-omnibus_2025.pdf?sfvrsn=ab89bee_1) and email us at [employment@sgenable.sg](mailto:employment@sgenable.sg), or

3)      Approach SG Enable’s Information and Career Centre, located within the Enabling Village, for assistance.

Jobseekers with disabilities can also apply for vacancies with our inclusive employers in our [Disability Employment Portal](https://eservice1.enable.gov.sg/MSFPortal/EDS/Employment/Pages/Common/Index/Index.aspx).

title: Hospital-to-Work Transition Programme
description: Provides case management, rehabilitation and employment support for persons with acquired disability from accidents or medical conditions who are looking to return to work.
highlights: Provides employment assistance for persons with acquired disabilities
Personalised rehabilitation and training facilitation
1-1 case management services

sections.About this support:
Jobseekers in the programme can get personalised career re-assessment, rehabilitation and job-matching services. Persons with disabilities who are already in employment can also benefit from job support services. A case manager will support you throughout your transition to work, providing the following services:

Rehabilitation

- For clients requiring rehabilitation support, SG Enable collaborates with partner agencies such as SPD and ABLE to provide integrated rehabilitation and employment support services.

Case management

- Assessing the jobseeker’s strengths, job interests and skills, and identifying job options.
- Facilitate psychosocial and community support through referrals, if needed.
- Recommending relevant training courses, building resume and strengthening interview skills.
- Assessing the nature of the job and its tasks for suitability.
- Assessing the built environment for accessibility.
- Working with employers to job redesign and recommend workplace modification, if needed.

Employment support

- Vocational re-assessment, training coordination, job matching and placement, and on-site job coaching to help the new employee integrate into the workplace.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Above 16 years of age
- Medically certified as fit for employment
- Persons with a permanent acquired disability*^ based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least one of the six Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - Moderate Visual Impairment or worse in the better eye
  - Moderate Hearing Loss or worse in the better ear

*If your condition does not fall under the categories listed above, you may still approach SG Enable for a discussion.

^You can check if your disability status is verified on [SupportGoWhere ](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/status/pwdr)by logging with your Singpass or contacting us at [H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg](mailto:H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg).
sections.How to apply?:
**Preparation of documents**

The following supporting documents are required before making an application:

- [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/disability-verification-form.pdf) (To be completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional)
- [Fitness for Employment and Rehabilitation Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/h2w-fitness-for-employment-and-rehabilitation-form.pdf) (To be completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional)
- [Hospital-to-Work Application Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/h2w-application-form.pdf) (For email/physical submissions only)
- [OneMSF Omnibus Consent Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/onemsf-omnibus-consent-form_version-1-0.docx)
- Copy of NRIC Front and Back

** For persons with disabilities**:

- Apply online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/h2w/apply), or
- Email [H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg](mailto:H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg) with the above completed supporting documents
- Approach SG Enable’s Information and Career Centre, located within the Enabling Village, for assistance.

** **

**For Healthcare Professionals (HCP) **making referrals:

- Email [H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg](mailto:H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg) with the above supporting documents filled and endorsed.

title: GRaduate Industry Traineeships @Gov (GRIT@Gov)
description: Equips fresh graduates with experience and skills, easing their transition into full-time employment.
highlights: 3 to 6-month traineeships in Public Service for fresh graduates
Enables fresh graduates to gain useful skills and experience through short-term traineeships
Trainees receive a monthly training allowance ranging from S$1,800 to $2,400

sections.About this support:
The GRaduate Industry Traineeships @Gov (GRIT@Gov) Programme supports fresh graduates in gaining experience and skills, to facilitate their transition into full-time employment. GRIT@Gov offers traineeships for fresh graduates within public sector agencies.

Trainees will receive a monthly training allowance ranging from S$1,800 to $2,400 for the duration of the traineeship. This training allowance may vary depending on the scope of each traineeship.
sections.Who is this for?:
All trainees must fulfil the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident; and
  - Graduated or graduating in 2024, 2025 or 2026 from Universities, Polytechnics, Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and other Educational Institutions (e.g. private universities and overseas institutions); or
  - Graduated earlier from above institutions and completed National Service in 2024, 2025 or 2026.** **
  - Applicants must have no prior working experience and must be prepared to commit to a full-time traineeship.

Trainees who complete their studies from Universities, Polytechnics, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) or other Educational Institutions within 2026 but who will only receive their qualification/certification award in 2027 are eligible for the programme as well.
sections.How to apply?:
Browse and apply for GRIT@Gov traineeships via [Careers@Gov](https://jobs.careers.gov.sg/?s=grit@gov&utm_source=c@gshopfront&utm_medium=click&utm_id=grit-gov).

If you are a fresh graduate who is considering a role in the Public Service, check out our [Early Careers](https://www.careers.gov.sg/join-us/early-careers/?utm_source=gritgovpage&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=gritgovprog) page.

To view all vacancies across the Public Service (including for mid-careerists), please visit our [Careers@Gov job portal](https://jobs.careers.gov.sg/?utm_source=gritgovpage&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=gritgovprog).

title: Tech Immersion and Placement Programme (TIPP)
description: Immersive training bootcamp to prepare non-ICT professionals for ICT roles like web developers, user experience designers, and data analysts.
highlights: Prepare mid-career professionals for a career switch into tech
Mentorship and coaching from leading experts in ICT field
Subsidised course fee upon completion of the programme

sections.About this support:
- [Immersive ICT training courses or mentorship & coaching programmes](https://www.imda.gov.sg/How-We-Can-Help/TechSkills-Accelerator-TeSA/Tech-Immersion-and-Placement-Programme-TIPP#Eligible-partners-and-courses) that will lead to the creation of an impressive portfolio
- Interact with leading experts
- Enjoy subsidised course fees
sections.Who is this for?:
- **Individuals: **Singapore Citizens who are non-ICT professionals and are interested in switching to ICT job roles
- **Companies: **Singapore registered Institute of Higher Learning (IHL); or Private Education Institution (PEI) with a valid Enhanced Registration Framework (ERF) registered with SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) for the duration of the project qualifying period.
- Other eligibility criteria varies by [industry partner and course.](https://www.imda.gov.sg/How-We-Can-Help/TechSkills-Accelerator-TeSA/Tech-Immersion-and-Placement-Programme-TIPP#Eligible-partners-and-courses)
sections.How to apply?: You can visit the list of [eligible partners and courses](https://www.imda.gov.sg/How-We-Can-Help/TechSkills-Accelerator-TeSA/Tech-Immersion-and-Placement-Programme-TIPP#Eligible-partners-and-courses) and apply directly via the partners' website

title: Company-Led Training (CLT) Programme
description: Deepen your tech and media skills through on-the-job training in emerging tech and media areas such as artificial intelligence, cyber security, data analytics and virtual production.
highlights: On-the-job training for in-demand tech and media skills
Work on projects guided by experienced mentors
Enhance your employability and career pathways in tech and media roles

sections.About this support:
- Gain employment and receive a salary while being equipped with in-demand tech and media skills
- Work on projects guided by experienced mentors
- Gain in-depth industry exposure
- Enhance your employability and career pathways in tech and media roles
sections.Who is this for?:
Participating organisations must:

- Be a Singapore-registered company.
- Employ professionals in tech and media job roles that are in demand by the industry.
- Have the capability and capacity to deliver training programmes, with a good track record in human resource development.
- Commit resources including practical projects and qualified mentors to support trainees’ learning.
- Provide structured career progression pathways based on skills and competencies.
- Ensure that Singapore Permanent Residents (SPRs) do not exceed 15% of total trainees who have completed training.
sections.How to apply?: You can visit the [list of eligible companies](https://www.imda.gov.sg/How-We-Can-Help/TechSkills-Accelerator-TeSA/Company-Led-Training-Programme-CLT/Full-List-of-Job-Roles) and apply via the partners' website.
